# Land automatically, revert in one call and honour path limits

## Intent

Landing in Parley is not serialized, so safety comes from what surrounds it. An agent must be able to mark a change to land by itself once policy is satisfied and walk away; a developer must be able to undo a landed change with one call when something breaks afterwards; a token limited to some paths must never create, land or revert work outside those paths; and only the workspace's owner, with a credential that is not confined to a workspace, may land past unmet approvals and checks. This package gives the hub those four behaviours on top of optimistic landing and landing policy.

## Goals

- A change with `auto_land: true` gets a land attempt with `trigger: "auto_land"` when it becomes `ready` and `clean`, with permission checked as the user who set the flag and events written with actor `system`.
- An automatic attempt that ends `conflict` or `blocked` keeps the flag; one that ends `failed` is retried after 2 s, doubling to at most 5 min, at most 10 times, and then the flag is cleared.
- In a stack a change is landed automatically only after the change below it has landed.
- `POST /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/changes/:number/revert` on a landed change creates the branch `revert/<number>` and opens a change that undoes the landed commits, or answers `409 revert_conflict` with a conflict report and creates nothing.
- `parley change revert <slug> <number>` does the same from the shell.
- A path-scoped token creates a version, lands, reverts and sets `auto_land` only when every file concerned matches one of its globs; otherwise `403 path_not_allowed` naming the path.
- `override` on a land call is accepted only from the workspace's owner with an API key or an unbound PAT, or from the admin token, while `land.allow_override` is true; it skips unmet approvals and checks, never a `block`, and is recorded.

## Requirements

All routes are under `/api/v1`. The conventions of package 02 apply (error envelope, order of checks, `Idempotency-Key`).

### Starting an automatic land (LAND-FR-060)

A change is landable when it is `open`, its `landing.status` is `ready` and its `mergeable` is `clean`. When a change with `auto_land: true` becomes landable, which package 23's announcement reports with exactly one `parley.change.ready` event per transition, `parleyd` starts a land attempt for that one change with `trigger: "auto_land"`, without `stack`, without `override` and with `session_id` null. The attempt's `requested_by` names the user who set the flag; its events (`parley.change.land`, `parley.change.land_fail`) have actor `system`.

Before the attempt starts, permission is checked as the user who set the flag, by LAND-FR-001: that user exists and is not blocked, and has write access to the target workspace or is the change's author while `land.by_author` is true. If the check fails, no attempt is created, the flag is cleared and one `parley.change.land_fail` is emitted on the change with `reason: "not_permitted"`, `status: "blocked"` and `land_id: null`.

Nothing is started when, at the moment the event is handled, the change is no longer `open`, the flag is off, the change is no longer landable, or a land attempt for the change is `running`. The same start is made when the flag is set to `true` on a change that is already landable, and at hub start for every change that is landable with the flag on and no `running` attempt.

### Outcomes and retries (LAND-FR-061)

- `landed`: nothing more to do.
- `conflict` or `blocked`: the flag stays on and no retry is scheduled; the next time the change becomes landable a new attempt is started.
- `failed`: a new attempt is started after a delay. The delays are 2 s, 4 s, 8 s, 16 s, 32 s, 64 s, 128 s, 256 s, 300 s, 300 s: at most 10 retries after the first failed attempt. When the 10th retry also ends `failed`, the flag is cleared and nothing more is started. Each retry is a new land attempt.

A retry that comes due while the change is not landable, not `open` or without the flag is dropped, and the retry count starts again from zero. The count also starts again after any attempt that does not end `failed`. The retry count and the due time are stored, so a retry that was pending when the hub stopped is made after the next start, at its due time or at once when that time has passed.

### Stacks (LAND-FR-062)

A change with `depends_on` naming a change that is not `landed` is never landed automatically: no attempt is started and the flag stays on. When the change below lands, the hub restacks the dependant (package 24); when the dependant then becomes landable it is landed automatically like any other change. An automatic attempt never lands a stack.

### Revert (LAND-FR-070, LAND-FR-071)

`POST /workspaces/:slug/changes/:number/revert` with body `{"title"?: string, "intent"?: string, "draft"?: bool, "auto_land"?: bool, "session_id"?: string}` on a landed change:

1. reads the head *T* of the original change's target branch;
2. builds, on *T*, one commit per landed commit of the original change, newest landed commit first, each undoing that commit. A reverting commit has the subject `Revert "<subject of the undone commit>"` and the body `This reverts commit <full id>.`; its author and committer are the hub's landing identity (`[land].committer_name`, `[land].committer_email`);
3. creates the branch `revert/<number>` in the target workspace at the last of those commits. When that branch exists, `revert/<number>-2` is used, then `-3`, and so on, the first name that is free;
4. opens a change with that branch as source, the original's target branch as target, `reverts: <number>`, a first version of kind `revert`, the caller as author, the title `Revert "<title of the original>"` (cut to 200 characters) unless `title` is given, and the intent `Reverts change <slug>#<number>: <title of the original>.` unless `intent` is given; `draft: true` opens it as a draft;
5. answers `201` with the new change.

The original change then shows `reverted_by: <new number>`. `parley.change.revert` is emitted on the original with `reverted_by`, with the caller as actor; the new change gets `parley.change.version` and, unless it is a draft, `parley.change.open`, as any opened change does. The branch creation is recorded as `parley.git.push` with `via: "api"`.

The reverting change is an ordinary change: policy is evaluated for it, it needs whatever its files need, and it lands through the ordinary land call. `auto_land: true` in the body sets the flag with the caller as the user who set it. Reverting a reverting change is allowed and restores the original content.

Failures, in this order after authentication, scope, access and the lookup of the change:

| Case | Answer |
|---|---|
| body member of the wrong type; `title` not 1 to 200 characters or with a line break; `intent` over 16,000 characters | `400 invalid_request` |
| `session_id` fails the session-linking rule | `400 unknown_session` |
| target workspace `archived` | `409 workspace_archived` |
| the change is not `landed` | `409 change_not_landed` |
| a `draft`, `open` or `landed` change already reverts it | `409 already_reverted`, with `details.reverted_by` |
| the original's target branch no longer exists | `400 target_not_found` |
| a file of the original change is outside a path-scoped caller's globs | `403 path_not_allowed`, with `path` |
| the original landed with `noop: true`, or every reverting commit would be empty | `400 nothing_to_land` |
| a landed commit can no longer be undone on *T* | `409 revert_conflict`, with a conflict report in `details.conflict` |

On every failure nothing is created: no branch, no change, no event. `reverted_by` is the highest-numbered change that reverts this one and is `draft`, `open` or `landed`; it is null when there is none, so an abandoned revert allows a new one.

### Who may revert (LAND-FR-072, LAND-FR-003)

Reverting needs `changes:write` on a PAT (`403 insufficient_scope` without it) and either write access to the target workspace, or being the author of the original change while `land.by_author` is true (`403 forbidden` otherwise). A caller without read access gets `404 not_found`; an unknown change number gets `404 change_not_found`. A token bound to a fork of the workspace gets `403 token_bound`: a fork token cannot revert on the parent.

### `parley change revert <slug> <number>`

Flags `--title`, `--intent`, `--draft`, `--auto-land`, `--session <id>`. It sends `POST /workspaces/:slug/changes/:number/revert` with the members the flags give, prints the new change as JSON on stdout and exits 0; a hub error prints the envelope on stderr and exits 1; a missing argument or a number that is not a positive integer is a usage error, exit 2, with no request sent.

### Path limits when a version is created (LAND-FR-080)

The files of a version are the paths that differ between its base and its head, a rename counting with both its old and its new path. They are computed from the repository, not from the change's stored `paths` list, which stops at 2,000. A credential with `paths` may create a version only when every one of those files matches at least one of its globs (the matcher of package 06 in `internal/identity`, not the policy matcher of package 27). The first file in byte order that matches none is named in the refusal. A credential without `paths` is never checked, and versions the hub creates on its own (a restack with actor `system`, a `sync` version) are not checked.

Package 18 checks the commits a push or an API write adds, and package 22 checks `POST …/changes`. This package covers what is left:

- **Updates that add no new commit.** A push, an API ref move or a rebase answered from existing commits that moves a branch which is the source of a `draft` or `open` change, or that opens a change, is checked against the files of the resulting version. This package supplies the push-rule engine's version-files lookup: given what the engine of package 18 passes (the slug, the branch, the new head and the flag that the update opens a change), it answers whether a version results and which files it has; for an update that opens a change the files are taken against the target branch that package 22's open defaults to. The engine refuses with rule 5 (`403 path_not_allowed` with `path` over the API; `path <path> is outside this token's allowed paths` over git), so a path-scoped token cannot adopt out-of-path commits made with another credential.
- **Restack.** `POST …/changes/:number/restack`, with or without `resolutions`, by a path-scoped caller is refused with `403 path_not_allowed` and `path` when a file of the version it would record is outside the globs; the source branch does not move and no version is recorded.

### Path limits at landing, revert and auto_land (LAND-FR-081, LAND-FR-082)

A path-scoped token may land a change, revert a change and set `auto_land: true` on a change only when every file of the change's current version matches its globs; otherwise `403 path_not_allowed` with `path`, and nothing changes: no land attempt is recorded, no branch or change is created, the flag keeps its value. For a land with `stack: true` every change the attempt would land is checked. For a revert the files are those of the landed version. Setting `auto_land` is checked wherever it can be set: `POST …/changes`, `PATCH …/changes/:number` and `POST …/revert`. Setting it to `false` is never refused.

When the flag is set with a path-scoped token, the token's globs are stored with the flag. When an automatic land is about to start, the files of the change's current version are checked against those stored globs; on a miss no attempt is created, the flag is cleared and `parley.change.land_fail` with `reason: "not_permitted"` is emitted, as for a user who may no longer land.

Path limits and policy are independent. A path-scoped token whose globs cover the change still gets `409 policy_blocked` when policy is not `ready`; a change whose policy is `ready` is still refused to a token whose globs do not cover it.

### Override (LAND-FR-002)

`POST …/changes/:number/land` may carry `override: {"reason": "<text>"}`. The shape of the member is checked by the land route of package 25 (first row). This package's refusals run as a request guard of that route, before a land attempt is created, whatever the policy status:

| Case | Answer |
|---|---|
| `override` is not an object, or `reason` is missing, not a string or empty after trimming white space | `400 invalid_request` (package 25) |
| the credential is a workspace-bound PAT (bound to the workspace or to a fork), whoever its user is | `403 override_not_allowed` |
| the caller is not the workspace's owner and not the admin token (a member with write access, an author landing by `land.by_author`) | `403 override_not_allowed` |
| the workspace setting `land.allow_override` is false, for every caller including the admin token | `403 override_not_allowed` |

An accepted override takes effect through the override rule this package registers beside the policy gate of package 25, for every change of the attempt: a change whose `landing.status` is `pending` passes. A change whose status is `blocked` (a `block` requirement or a structural reason) still ends the attempt `blocked` with `409 policy_blocked`. When at least one change passed only because of the override, the land attempt's `override` is `{"reason": …}` and each `parley.change.land` event carries it in `override`; when every change was `ready` anyway, `override` is null.

### End-to-end flows

1. An agent opens a change with `auto_land: true` in a workspace whose policy requires the check `test`. `parleyd` evaluates it `pending`. A developer's runner reports `test` as `passed`; `parleyd` re-evaluates, announces the change landable, starts a land attempt with `trigger: "auto_land"` and lands it. The agent reads the change: `landed`.
2. A developer runs `parley change revert demo 7`. The parley CLI posts to the revert route; `parleyd` builds the reverting commits, creates `revert/7`, opens change 8 with `reverts: 7` and answers `201`. The developer lands change 8; the target branch has the content it had before change 7 landed.
3. An agent holding a token with `paths: ["docs/**"]` asks to land a change that touches `src/main.go`; `parleyd` answers `403 path_not_allowed` naming `src/main.go` and records no attempt. The agent lands a change that touches only `docs/a.md` with the same token; it lands.

## Design Decisions

1. **Profile: full.** Three flows cross the CLI, the routes, the land component, the repository and the event log.
2. **Language Go; git through `internal/gitrepo` as a subprocess; SQLite behind `internal/store`; `net/http`; cobra for the CLI; a replaceable clock.** Project-wide decisions. The backoff tests rely on the clock.
3. **The override rules are this package's; the land call is package 25's.** The plan names LAND-FR-002's override rules here. Package 25 declares two registration points for them in `internal/land` and this package fills both from `internal/land/override.go`: a request guard, asked before the preconditions, that answers `403 override_not_allowed`; and the override rule, asked by the engine for a gate answer that is not `ready`, that lets `pending` pass and nothing else. Package 25 validates the member's shape, records `override` when the rule let a change pass, and package 27's gate knows nothing of overrides.
4. **Any `override` from a caller who may not override is refused, even when policy is `ready`.** LAND-FR-002 says a bound PAT "can never override"; one rule is simpler than one that depends on policy.
5. **`land.allow_override: false` answers `403 override_not_allowed` to everyone, the admin token included.** The PRD says only that overrides "can be disabled per workspace".
6. **"Owner" is the access level `owner` of package 07**, as in package 18.
7. **`reason` must be a non-empty string; no other limit.** The PRD gives none; the request body limit of package 02 bounds it.
8. **`override` is recorded only when it let a change pass**, following the land attempt field "`{reason}` when policy was overridden".
9. **`not_permitted` without an attempt is reported as `parley.change.land_fail` with `status: "blocked"` and `land_id: null`.** The catalogue allows three statuses and no attempt exists.
10. **A failed path check at the start of an automatic land is handled as `not_permitted`.** LAND-FR-081 says it is "checked the same way" and names no other outcome.
11. **The globs and the credential type are stored when the flag is set, by package 23 (with packages 22 and 23).** The flag has one store: `SetAutoLand` of `internal/change`, which the `Open` of package 22 and the `PATCH` of package 23 both call, stores the setter (user, credential type, token globs) beside the flag, and package 23 exposes it through the accessor `AutoLandSetter`. This package keeps no setter row; its own table holds only the retry count and the due time of a pending retry, and it clears the flag through the same `SetAutoLand`. `paths` is fixed at creation, so the copy is exact, and the check still works after the token is revoked or expires. `requested_by` of an automatic attempt is `{actor_type: <that credential type>, actor_id, username}` of the user who set the flag.
12. **The user-level check at start does not look at scopes.** The credential had `changes:write` when it set the flag; LAND-FR-060 says "checked as the user". A flag set with the admin token is always permitted.
13. **Setting the flag on an already landable change, and hub start, start an attempt.** Otherwise such a change waits for a transition that never comes (LAND-US-07); the PRD names only the transition.
14. **"Up to 10 times" means 10 retries after the first failed attempt**, 11 attempts in all, and the count restarts after any other outcome.
15. **A due retry is dropped when the change is not landable.** The next landable announcement starts a fresh attempt.
16. **Automatic landing never uses `stack: true`**, so LAND-FR-062 holds by one rule: no attempt while `depends_on` names an unlanded change.
17. **Reverting commits are authored and committed by the hub's landing identity**, with git's usual revert message. The PRD does not say; the caller is recorded as the change's author and the version's creator.
18. **The default intent is `Reverts change <slug>#<number>: <title>.`** The PRD asks only that it name the original.
19. **A draft reverting change counts for `already_reverted` and `reverted_by`; an abandoned one does not.** `draft: true` is a body option, and two live reverts of one change would conflict with each other.
20. **Nothing to undo is `400 nothing_to_land`**, the answer an open with no commits gets (CHG-FR-003).
21. **The revert branch is created as an API ref creation of package 18**: `Evaluate` of the push rule engine in `internal/gitserver/pushrule` with the caller's facts, then `Apply`, its ref writer, with `via: "api"` (the writer accepts only `git`, `api` and `land`), so every branch movement is one `parley.git.push`. A refusal by a push rule (for example a protected-branch glob that covers `revert/*`) is answered as package 21 answers it, `403` with the rule's `error_type`, and nothing is created.
22. **The path check at landing runs before the preconditions of LAND-FR-010 and creates no attempt.** The PRD gives it no position; a refusal that does not depend on state should not leave a record.
23. **Wiring.** Everything this package adds to another package goes through a registration point the owner declares. With `internal/land` (package 25): the override rule, request guards, a final observer and the start function for trigger `auto_land`. With the push-rule engine (package 18): its version-files lookup. With `internal/change`: an `auto_land` guard (the `AutoLandGuard` package 22 declares, registered with `RegisterAutoLandGuard`), called by the open of package 22 and the `PATCH` of package 23 before the flag is stored as `true`, with the caller's credential and the change; and a version guard (the `VersionGuard` package 24 declares, registered with `RegisterVersionGuard`), called by the manual restack of package 24 after the replay is computed and before the source branch moves, with the caller's credential and the base and head of the version to record. The landable trigger needs no registration: the automatic lander reads `parley.change.ready` events after a stored position through `ReadAfter` of the event component (package 52), so each event starts at most one attempt and none is lost over a restart.
24. **The revert's conflict report** is `ConflictReport`, the one conflict report type (declared by package 20 in `internal/gitrepo/conflictreport.go`, used by landing); `landed_changes` and every `landed_by` are empty and `change` is null.

## Dependencies

- Package 25 optimistic_landing (draft): land attempts, the land call and its policy gate, the landed commits of a change.
- Package 27 landing_policy (draft): `landing.status` per change, which the automatic lander reads, and the policy gate whose answers the override rule judges.
- Package 24 change_stacks_and_restack (draft): the manual restack, which calls the version guard this package registers.
- Package 09 cli_foundation (draft): the command helper and client `parley change revert` is built on.
- Package 52 durable_event_log_and_stream (draft): the event writer for `parley.change.revert` and `parley.change.land_fail`.
- Through them: packages 02, 06, 07, 08, 18, 20, 22 and 23.
- The `git` command, 2.38 or later, at run time.

## Glossary

- **Workspace**: A repository the hub holds, identified by its `slug`. Either a registered repository or a task fork.
- **Change**: The unit of work: a proposal to add the commits of a source branch to a target branch, with a number, a title, an intent, versions and a state.
- **Version**: One head of a change's source branch. Every push, API commit or restack that moves the source creates a new version. Old versions stay fetchable.
- **Stack**: Changes linked by `depends_on`, lowest first.
- **Restack**: The hub rebasing a dependent change onto the new head of the change below it, or onto the target once that change has landed.
- **Landing**: Adding a change's commits to its target branch: a server-side rebase followed by a compare-and-swap of the target ref.
- **Land attempt**: One request to land a change (or a stack), with its outcome.
- **Conflict report**: The structured description of why a rebase could not be done: files, kinds, and the landed changes involved.
- **Policy**: A workspace's ordered rules that map touched paths to landing requirements.
- **Bound token**: A PAT confined to one workspace (and the forks created with it).
- **Path-scoped token**: A PAT whose writes are limited to files matching a list of globs.
- **Hub event**: A record of something the hub did (`parley.*` types), with a sequence number.
- **Landable**: A change that is `open`, with `landing.status` `ready` and `mergeable` `clean`.
- **Setter**: The user whose credential last set `auto_land` to `true` on a change.

# Requirements

## Requirements

### REQ-1: Start an automatic land when a change becomes landable

**Rationale:** An agent sets auto_land and walks away; the hub lands the change as soon as policy is satisfied, with the permissions of the user who asked (LAND-FR-060).

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-1.1] WHEN an open change with auto_land true becomes landable (landing.status ready and mergeable clean) and the user who set the flag may land it, THE parleyd SHALL start one land attempt for that change alone with trigger auto_land, without stack, without override and with session_id null
   → a land attempt exists with trigger "auto_land", changes [<number>], override null, session_id null and requested_by {actor_type: the credential type the flag was set with, actor_id and username of the user who set it}; the parley.change.land or parley.change.land_fail event of the attempt has actor_type "system" and actor_id null
   Check: integration
   - setup: a workspace whose policy requires the check test, with a real repository created by git init in t.TempDir()
   - setup: an open change with auto_land true and the check not yet reported
   ```
   in internal/land/autoland_test.go, a table over the setter {workspace owner with an API key, org member who authored the change with land.by_author true and a PAT, admin token}: report the check passed so that the re-evaluation writes one parley.change.ready; wait for the attempt; run the lander's pass over the event log twice; assert lands(change) has exactly one attempt with trigger == 'auto_land', changes == [n], override == nil, session_id == nil, requested_by matching the setter; assert change.state == 'landed'; assert the parley.change.land event has actor_type == 'system' and metadata.trigger == 'auto_land'
   ```
1. [REQ-1.2] IF a change with auto_land true becomes landable and the user who set the flag may not land it at that moment (the user is deleted, the user is blocked, the user lost write access and is not the author, or the user is the author without write access and land.by_author is false), THEN THE parleyd SHALL create no land attempt, clear the flag and emit one parley.change.land_fail event on the change
   → the change stays open with auto_land false; no land attempt is recorded; exactly one parley.change.land_fail event with actor_type "system" and metadata {land_id: null, status: "blocked", reason: "not_permitted"}; the target branch is unchanged
   Check: integration
   ```

### REQ-2: Keep, retry or clear auto_land by the outcome of the attempt

**Rationale:** A conflict or a policy block waits for the author; a transient failure is retried without anyone watching, and not forever (LAND-FR-061).

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-2.1] WHEN an automatic land attempt ends conflict or blocked, THE parleyd SHALL leave auto_land on, schedule no retry, and start a new attempt the next time the change becomes landable
   → auto_land stays true; no further land attempt is recorded while the change is not landable, however much time passes; one new attempt with trigger "auto_land" is recorded after the change becomes landable again
   Check: integration
   - setup: a fake clock
   - setup: a change with auto_land true whose automatic attempt ends conflict because another change landed first on the same lines
   ```
   in internal/land/autoland_test.go: assert change.auto_land == true and len(lands) == 1; advance the clock 1 hour; assert len(lands) == 1; push a version that resolves the conflict so the change becomes landable; wait; assert len(lands) == 2 and change.state == 'landed'. Second case with a stub land component that ends 'blocked': same assertions up to the advance
   ```
1. [REQ-2.2] WHEN an automatic land attempt ends failed and fewer than 10 retries have been made since the last attempt that did not end failed, THE parleyd SHALL start a new automatic land attempt after a delay that is 2 seconds for the first retry and doubles for each further retry up to 300 seconds
   → the delays before retries 1 to 10 are 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 300 and 300 seconds; each retry is a new land attempt with trigger "auto_land"; auto_land stays true
   Check: unit
   - setup: a fake clock
   - setup: a stub land component whose attempts end failed with error contention
   ```
   in internal/land/autoland_test.go: start the first attempt; for each expected delay d in [2,4,8,16,32,64,128,256,300,300] seconds: advance the clock by d minus 1 ms and assert no new start; advance 1 ms and assert exactly one new start; assert the flag is still true while the tenth retry runs; when the tenth retry ends failed assert 11 starts in all, the flag is false, and advancing the clock 1 hour brings no further start
   ```
1. [REQ-2.3] IF the tenth retry of an automatic land also ends failed, THEN THE parleyd SHALL clear auto_land and start no further attempt
   → 11 land attempts with trigger "auto_land" and status failed are recorded for the change; auto_land is false; no retry is pending; the change stays open
   Check: same as REQ-2.2
1. [REQ-2.4] IF a retry comes due and the change is not open, its auto_land is false or it is not landable, THEN THE parleyd SHALL drop the retry and set the retry count to zero
   → no land attempt is started at the due time; auto_land keeps its value; a later failed series for the change starts again with a 2-second delay
   Check: unit
   - setup: a fake clock
   - setup: a stub land component
   ```
   in internal/land/autoland_test.go, a table over {change abandoned, flag set to false by PATCH, mergeable turned conflict} applied after the third failed attempt: advance past the due time; assert no new start; make the change landable again with the flag on and let the attempt fail; assert the next retry starts after 2 seconds
   ```
1. [REQ-2.5] WHEN an automatic land attempt ends with a status other than failed, THE parleyd SHALL set the retry count of the change to zero
   → the first retry after the next failed attempt is delayed 2 seconds, whatever the count was before
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/land/autoland_test.go with a fake clock and a stub land component: let attempts end failed, failed, conflict; make the change landable again and let the attempt end failed; assert the next start comes 2 seconds later, not 8
   ```
1. [REQ-2.6] WHEN parleyd starts while a retry of an automatic land is pending, THE parleyd SHALL make that retry at its due time, or at once when the due time has passed, with the stored retry count
   → exactly one new land attempt with trigger "auto_land" is started for the change, and the delay after it, should it fail, continues the stored sequence
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/land/autoland_test.go with a fake clock and a real store: let two attempts fail so a retry is pending 4 seconds out; stop the lander; advance 10 seconds; start a new lander on the same store with a stub land component that fails; assert one start at once; assert the following retry is due 8 seconds later
   ```

### REQ-3: Land a stack automatically from the bottom up

**Rationale:** A change cannot land before the change it depends on, so automatic landing waits for the one below (LAND-FR-062).

   → no land attempt is recorded for the upper change, its auto_land stays true and no parley.change.land_fail event is emitted for it
   Check: integration
   - setup: a stack of two changes; the upper has auto_land true and is ready and clean; the lower has auto_land false
   ```

   ```
1. [REQ-3.2] WHEN the change below has landed and the dependant with auto_land true, restacked by the hub, becomes landable, THE parleyd SHALL start an automatic land attempt for the dependant
   → the dependant ends landed by an attempt with trigger "auto_land" created after the lower change's attempt finished; the target branch holds the lower change's commits below the dependant's
   Check: integration
   - setup: a stack of two changes, both with auto_land true, both waiting for the check test
   ```
   in internal/land/autoland_test.go: report the check passed on the upper change first, then on the lower; wait until both are landed; assert each change has its own attempt with len(changes) == 1; assert lowerAttempt.finished_at <= upperAttempt.created_at; assert git log of the target lists the lower change's commit before the upper's
   ```
1. [REQ-3.3] THE parleyd SHALL for any land attempt with trigger auto_land, land exactly one change and never a stack
   Check: same as REQ-3.2

### REQ-4: Revert a landed change with one call

**Rationale:** When something breaks after landing, a developer needs the undo as an ordinary change, without a clone (LAND-FR-070, LAND-FR-071).

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-4.1] WHEN a caller who may revert sends POST /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/changes/:number/revert with an empty body for a landed change, THE parleyd SHALL build on the head of the original's target branch one commit per landed commit of the original, newest landed commit first, each undoing that commit, create the branch revert/<number> at the last of them and open a change from that branch to the original's target branch
   → HTTP 201 with the new change object: reverts == <number>, source {workspace_slug: <slug>, branch: "revert/<number>"}, target_branch equal to the original's, state "open", author the caller, version 1 of kind "revert", title `Revert "<original title>"` cut to 200 characters, intent `Reverts change <slug>#<number>: <original title>.`; each reverting commit has the subject `Revert "<subject>"`, the body `This reverts commit <40-character id>.` and the hub's landing identity as author and committer; the tree of the branch head equals the tree the target had before the original landed when nothing else landed since
   Check: integration
   - setup: a workspace with a real repository; a change with two commits landed with strategy rebase
   - setup: a second case landed with strategy squash
   ```
   in internal/land/revert_test.go: before = tree(target before landing); r = POST revert {}; assert r.status == 201; c = r.json; assert c.reverts == n, c.source.branch == 'revert/' + n, c.target_branch == orig.target_branch, c.state == 'open', c.title == 'Revert "' + orig.title + '"', c.intent names orig; assert versions(c)[0].kind == 'revert'; assert git log revert/n has 2 commits (1 for squash) on top of the target head, undoing the newest landed commit first, with the revert subject, body and the configured committer; assert tree(revert/n) == before. A row with a 200-character original title asserts len(c.title) == 200
   ```
1. [REQ-4.2] WHEN the revert request carries title, intent, draft, auto_land or session_id, THE parleyd SHALL open the reverting change with the given title and intent, as a draft when draft is true, with auto_land set by the caller when auto_land is true, and linked to the given session
   → HTTP 201; the change has the given title and intent; with draft true its state is "draft" and no parley.change.open event is written; with auto_land true its auto_land is true and the caller is the user who set it; session_id is the given id
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/land/revert_test.go, a table over bodies {title+intent, draft true, auto_land true, session_id of a session of the caller}: assert 201 and the corresponding fields; for draft assert no parley.change.open event; for auto_land in a workspace with the default policy assert the reverting change is landed by an attempt with trigger 'auto_land'
   ```
1. [REQ-4.3] WHEN the branch revert/<number> already exists in the target workspace when a revert is accepted, THE parleyd SHALL create the branch under the first free name among revert/<number>-2, revert/<number>-3 and so on
   → HTTP 201 with source.branch "revert/<number>-2" when only revert/<number> exists and "revert/<number>-3" when revert/<number>-2 exists too; the existing branches are not moved
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/land/revert_test.go: create branch revert/7 by hand; revert change 7; assert source.branch == 'revert/7-2' and head(revert/7) unchanged; abandon that change, keep its branch, revert again; assert source.branch == 'revert/7-3'
   ```
1. [REQ-4.4] WHEN a revert has opened its change, THE parleyd SHALL record the events of the revert and show the reverting change on the original
   → the original change reads reverted_by == <new number>; one parley.change.revert event on the original with the caller as actor and metadata {reverted_by: <new number>}; one parley.change.version event with kind "revert" on the new change and, unless it is a draft, one parley.change.open; one parley.git.push event for refs/heads/revert/<number> with created true and via "api"
   Check: integration
   ```

   ```
1. [REQ-4.5] IF a revert request is malformed or cannot apply: a body member of the wrong type, a title that is not 1 to 200 characters or has a line break, an intent over 16,000 characters, a session_id that fails the session-linking rule, an archived target workspace, a change that is not landed, a change that a draft, open or landed change already reverts, a target branch that no longer exists, or nothing to undo (the original landed with noop true or every reverting commit would be empty), THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request with the first failing case in that order and create nothing
   → HTTP 400 invalid_request; 400 unknown_session; 409 workspace_archived; 409 change_not_landed; 409 already_reverted with details.reverted_by the number of the reverting change; 400 target_not_found; 400 nothing_to_land, in that order of cases; in every case no branch, no change, no version and no event is created
   Check: integration

One more row combines an invalid title with an unlanded change and asserts invalid_request
   ```

   ```

   → HTTP 403 insufficient_scope; 403 forbidden; 403 forbidden; 403 token_bound; 404 not_found; 404 change_not_found, in that order of cases; no branch, change or event is created
   Check: integration

   ```
1. [REQ-5.2] WHEN the revert route is called with changes:write by a caller with write access to the target workspace, by the admin token, or by the original change's author without write access while land.by_author is true, THE parleyd SHALL accept the revert
   → HTTP 201 with the reverting change, whose author is the caller
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/land/revert_test.go, a table over {owner API key, member of the org with write access through a PAT with changes:write, admin token, org member who authored the change from a fork and uses an API key}: assert 201
   ```

   → HTTP 409 policy_blocked with the land attempt in details when policy is not ready; HTTP 200 with a landed attempt when policy is ready
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/land/pathlimit_test.go: policy requires the check test for docs/**; a token limited to docs/** lands a change touching docs/a.md: assert 409 policy_blocked with details holding the attempt and its requirements; report the check passed; land again: assert 200 and status 'landed'
   ```

### REQ-9: Let only the workspace owner land past unmet approvals and checks

**Rationale:** An override is the one way past policy; it must be out of reach of any agent token and leave a record (LAND-FR-002).

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-9.1] WHEN the workspace's owner with an API key or an unbound PAT, or the admin token, calls the land route with override {reason} while land.allow_override is true and at least one change of the attempt has landing.status pending, THE parleyd SHALL let every pending change pass the policy gate, land, and record the override
   → HTTP 200 with a landed attempt whose override is {reason: <the given text>}; each parley.change.land event of the attempt carries metadata.override {reason: <the given text>}
   Check: integration
   - setup: a policy requiring one approval and the check test; none given
   ```
   in internal/land/override_test.go, a table over callers {owner API key, owner unbound PAT with changes:write, admin token} and shapes {single change, stack true with two pending changes}: r = POST land {override: {reason: 'hotfix'}}; assert 200, status 'landed', attempt.override.reason == 'hotfix'; assert every land event has metadata.override.reason == 'hotfix'
   ```
1. [REQ-9.2] IF an accepted override is given and a change of the attempt has landing.status blocked, by a block requirement or by a structural reason, THEN THE parleyd SHALL end the attempt blocked without moving the target
   → HTTP 409 with error_type policy_blocked and the land attempt in details, with status "blocked", blocked naming the change and override null; the target branch is unchanged
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/land/override_test.go: policy rule {paths: ['deploy/secrets/**'], require: {block: true}}; the owner lands a change touching deploy/secrets/k with override; assert 409 policy_blocked, details.status == 'blocked', details.override == nil, head(target) unchanged. Second row: a draft change with override -> not landed
   ```
1. [REQ-9.3] IF a land call carries a well-formed override and the credential is a PAT bound to the workspace or to one of its forks, or the caller is neither the workspace's owner nor the admin token, or the workspace setting land.allow_override is false, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the call before a land attempt is created, whatever the policy status of the change
   → HTTP 403 with error_type override_not_allowed; no land attempt is recorded; the target branch is unchanged
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/land/override_test.go, a table over {the owner's PAT bound to the workspace, a fork-bound PAT of the owner landing a change from that fork, a member of the org with write access using an API key, the change's author landing by land.by_author, the owner's API key with land.allow_override false, the admin token with land.allow_override false} crossed with policy {pending, ready}: r = POST land {override: {reason: 'x'}}; assert 403 and error_type == 'override_not_allowed'; assert lands is empty and head(target) unchanged; a malformed override ({reason: ''}) from the same callers is answered 400 invalid_request by the land route of package 25 before this refusal
   ```
1. [REQ-9.4] WHEN an accepted override is given and every change of the attempt has landing.status ready, THE parleyd SHALL land as without an override and record none
   → HTTP 200 with a landed attempt whose override is null; the parley.change.land event carries metadata.override null
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/land/override_test.go: default policy; the owner lands with override {reason: 'x'}; assert 200, attempt.override == nil, event metadata.override == nil
   ```

## Execution Paths

### PATH-1: A change with auto_land lands by itself once its required check passes

1. **agent** opens a change with auto_land true in a workspace whose policy requires the check test
2. **parleyd** evaluates the change as pending and starts nothing
3. **developer** reports the check test as passed on the change's version
4. **parleyd** re-evaluates the change as ready, writes one parley.change.ready through the landable announcement, reads that event and starts a land attempt with trigger auto_land as the user who set the flag
5. **parleyd** lands the change and writes parley.change.land with actor system
6. **agent** reads the change and sees state landed

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** parleyd HTTP server, change component, policy evaluation, land component, automatic lander, git repository on disk, store, event log

**Setup:**

- a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 with a workspace cloned from a test origin
- a policy with default {approvals: 0, checks: ["test"]}

**End state:**

- the change is landed and the target branch contains its commit
- the only land attempt of the change has trigger auto_land and status landed
- the event log holds parley.change.land for the change with actor_type system

**Pseudocode:**

```
in test/e2e/autoland_revert_test.go: commit a file through the API on a branch; POST changes {auto_land: true}; assert landing.status == 'pending'; PUT checks/test {status: 'passed'}; poll GET change until state == 'landed' (10 s limit); assert GET lands has one attempt with trigger 'auto_land'; assert the event log entry
```

### PATH-2: A developer reverts a landed change from the shell and lands the revert

1. **developer** runs parley change revert demo 7
2. **parley CLI** sends POST /api/v1/workspaces/demo/changes/7/revert
3. **parleyd** builds the reverting commits on the target head, creates the branch revert/7 and opens a change with reverts 7
4. **parleyd** answers 201 and writes parley.change.revert on change 7
5. **parley CLI** prints the new change and exits 0
6. **developer** lands the reverting change and reads the target branch with the content it had before change 7

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** parley CLI, parleyd HTTP server, revert operation, change component, land component, git repository on disk, event log

**Setup:**

- a hub started in-process with a workspace in which a change that edits one file has landed

**End state:**

- the CLI exited 0 and printed a change with reverts equal to the landed change's number
- the branch revert/<number> exists in the workspace
- after the reverting change lands, the file on the target branch has its content from before the original change
- the original change shows reverted_by and the event log holds parley.change.revert

**Pseudocode:**

```
in test/e2e/autoland_revert_test.go: before = file content on main; land a change editing the file; code = cli.Run(['change','revert',slug,n]); assert code == 0 and stdout JSON has reverts == n; git ls-remote shows refs/heads/revert/n; cli.Run(['change','land',slug,m]); assert the file read through the API equals before; assert GET change n has reverted_by == m
```

### PATH-3: A path-scoped token lands inside its paths and is refused outside them

1. **agent** asks to land a change that touches src/main.go with a token limited to docs/**
2. **parleyd** compares the files of the change's version with the token's globs and answers 403 path_not_allowed naming src/main.go, recording no attempt
3. **agent** asks to land a change that touches only docs/a.md with the same token
4. **parleyd** passes the path check, evaluates policy and lands the change

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** parleyd HTTP server, authentication with a real path-scoped PAT, path-limit check, land component, git repository on disk

**Setup:**

- a hub started in-process; the workspace owner minted a PAT with changes:write and paths ["docs/**"]
- two open changes made with the owner's API key: one touching src/main.go, one touching docs/a.md

**End state:**

- the first land answered 403 path_not_allowed with path src/main.go and that change has no land attempt
- the second change is landed

**Pseudocode:**

```
in test/e2e/path_limits_test.go: r1 = POST land of the src change with the PAT; assert 403, error_type 'path_not_allowed', error.path == 'src/main.go', GET lands empty; r2 = POST land of the docs change; assert 200 and status 'landed'
```


# Tasks

## Test Commands

- **all_tests:** `go test ./... -count=1`
- **linter:** `golangci-lint run ./...`
- **spec_tests:** `go test ./internal/land/... ./internal/cli/... ./test/e2e/... -count=1`

## Dependencies

- `09` — parley change revert is declared through its command helper and uses its HTTP client, output and exit codes
- `24` — registers the version guard that its manual restack calls before it moves the source branch
- `25` — starts land attempts through its start function, reads the landed commits of a change, and registers the override rule, the request guards and a final observer that internal/land declares
- `27` — reads the landing status it evaluates for each change, which the automatic lander acts on and the override rule judges
- `52` — writes parley.change.revert and parley.change.land_fail through its event component and reads parley.change.ready events after a position through ReadAfter

### 1. Check a version's files against a token's globs and answer the push rules' lookup (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-7.1, REQ-7.2, REQ-7.3, REQ-7.4

**Steps:**

- 1.1 Add the behaviours to internal/land/pathlimit_test.go (the glob and version table, the unrestricted and hub-made cases, the ref move onto existing commits, the lookup table) and the git push case to test/e2e/path_limits_test.go, and confirm they fail
- 1.2 Create internal/land/pathlimit.go with the path-limit check: given a credential's globs, a repository, a base commit and a head commit, list the paths that differ between base and head through internal/gitrepo with rename detection, counting a rename with both paths, sort them in byte order and return allowed, or refused with the first path that matches no glob; use the glob matcher package 06 exports from internal/identity ('?' literal), write no second matcher and never use the policy path matcher of package 27 here
- 1.3 Read the files from the repository on every call; never use the paths list stored on the change, which stops at 2,000
- 1.4 Answer allowed without reading the repository when the credential has no paths or the version is made by the hub with actor system
- 1.5 Return an error, not a refusal, when git fails, so that the caller answers an internal error instead of allowing or naming a path
- 1.6 Implement the version-files lookup the push-rule engine of package 18 declares in internal/gitserver/pushrule, with the arguments the engine passes (the slug, the branch, the new head and the opens-change flag): answer no version when the branch is not the source of a draft or open change and the flag is not set; otherwise answer the files between the merge base of the target head and the new head, the target being the change's, or for an update that opens a change the branch package 22's open defaults to
- 1.7 Register the lookup with the engine where parleyd wires its collaborators, so that a push or an API ref move that adds no new commit is refused by rule 5 with the first offending path

### 4. Start an automatic land when a change with auto_land becomes landable (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-1, REQ-8.3, REQ-8.4, REQ-8.5

**Steps:**

- 4.1 Add the start table, the not-permitted table, the nothing-to-start table, the set-while-landable case, the start-up case and the stored-globs cases to internal/land/autoland_test.go, and the PATCH cases to internal/land/pathlimit_test.go, and confirm they fail
- 4.2 Create internal/land/autoland.go with the automatic lander and a store table keyed by workspace and change number that holds, for a flag that is on, the retry count and the due time of a pending retry; the user who set the flag, the credential type and the credential's globs or null are not stored here: read them through the accessor AutoLandSetter of package 23, the one store of the setter
- 4.3 Register an auto_land guard with internal/change through RegisterAutoLandGuard, as the AutoLandGuard that package 22 declares and that the open of package 22 and the PATCH of package 23 call with the caller's credential and the change before they store auto_land true (revert reaches it through the open): for a path-scoped credential run the path-limit check on the change's current version and refuse with 403 path_not_allowed and the path, so that no member of the request is applied; otherwise accept, and record no setter: the caller stores the flag and its setter through SetAutoLand of internal/change (packages 22 and 23); setting false is never refused and deletes this package's retry row
- 4.4 Follow parley.change.ready, whose one writer is the landable announcement of package 23: read the events after a stored position with ReadAfter of the event component of package 52, run the start procedure for the change of each parley.change.ready event, and store the new position in the same transaction as the work it caused; a pass runs every second (the interval is a parameter) and is callable from tests; also run the start procedure when the guard has just accepted the flag on a change that is already landable
- 4.5 Start procedure: do nothing when the change is not open, the flag is off, the change is not landable, a land attempt for it is running, or its depends_on names a change that is not landed
- 4.6 Then check permission as the setter: the admin token passes; a user must exist, not be blocked, and have write access to the target workspace or be the change's author while land.by_author is true; scopes are not examined
- 4.7 Then, when the setter read through AutoLandSetter has globs, run the path-limit check on the change's current version against them, whether or not the token still exists
- 4.8 When either check fails, create no attempt, clear the flag through SetAutoLand of internal/change (which clears the stored setter), delete the retry row, and emit parley.change.land_fail on the change through the event component with actor system and metadata land_id null, status blocked, reason not_permitted
- 4.9 Otherwise start a land attempt for the one change through the start function package 25 exports for trigger auto_land, with no stack, no override, session_id null, requested_by built from the credential type and the user that AutoLandSetter returns, and system as the actor of its events
- 4.10 At start-up, after the land component has recovered its running attempts, run the start procedure for every open change with the flag on
- 4.11 Run the lander's work off the request path, stop it with the server's shutdown, and take the clock as a parameter
